newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Poh Lian offers 54 million new shares in IPO.
newsitem.headline: Poh Lian offers 54 million new shares in IPO.

text.p: Construction group Poh Lian Holdings Ltd said on Tuesday it was offering 54 million new shares at Singapore S$0.42 each in its initial public offering.
Poh Lian is one of Singapore's major providers of construction equipment.
The offer comprises 45.9 million shares for the public and 8.1 million placement shares. The shares are priced at a historic price earnings ratio of 10.63 times.
"This offer will raise about S$21 million to support our efforts to realise our expanson plans," said Tan Eng Khiam, chief executive officer of Poh Lian in a statement.
For the financial year ended December 31, 1996, Poh Lian made net profits of S$6.38 million on a turnover of S$182.76 million.
The company said it was confident of good growth prospects due to projected steady growth and current favourable outlook for the Singapore construction industry.
Its key growth strategy was regionalisation which includes plans to expand selected operations in Malaysia and China.
Areas in which it has identified for regional expansion are industrial property development, access equipment leasing, and building materials trading.
Poh Lian intends to seek joint ventures in Malaysia and China.

The group said the net proceeds from the share offer would be used to invest in two regional joint ventures - a construction and access equipment company in Malaysia and a construction and property development company in China.
The offer closes on May 13 and starts trading on May 15.
